title: Newborn immunisation against respiratory virus could cut infant winter hospitalisations
content: As the cold season nears, a new EU report indicates that universal immunisation of newborns against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) can reduce the risk of hospitalisation due to respiratory infections in young children by more than half.

title: Protecting Europe with stronger climate-resilience
content: The new EU framework for climate resilience strengthens Europe's ability to anticipate, prepare for, and manage climate risks. It does so by taking a proactive and systemic risk management approach and includes a new climate resilience law and practical tools.

title: A stronger Frontex for better protection of the EU’s external borders
content: The Commission has proposed to reinforce Frontex to help EU and Schengen countries manage the EU’s external borders more effectively. The new rules will give it the right tools and resources to act faster and support third countries on returns.

title: EU citizens think innovative foods can be useful but want more information, new Eurobarometer shows
content: The survey shows that many Europeans see food innovation as useful to help farmers and food producers respond to major challenges. Innovative foods can strengthen the resilience and preparedness of our food system, widen production options, support food security and help meet consumer needs.

content: The 2026 Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought has been collectively awarded to the International Criminal Court and its officials. With the award, the European Parliament ‘recognises the Court’s important work in upholding international law and justice’, said President Roberta Metsola.

title: Investigation into migration deal between Italy and Albania wins 2026 Daphne Caruana Galizia Prize for Journalism
content: An investigation into the migration deal between Italy and Albania has won the 2026 Daphne Caruana Galizia Prize. content: The Arctic is changing fast. From climate change to geopolitical tensions, there are challenges reshaping its security and economic landscape. title: Commission invests €3.4 billion in net-zero technology projects to decarbonise Europe
content: The Commission is reinvesting €3.4 billion of revenues from the EU ETS into more than 70 net-zero technology projects across Europe. These projects, in sectors like renewable energy and critical raw materials processing, will contribute to the EU’s clean transition, energy independence and security.

content: The European Commission has granted more than €390 million to 135 new climate and environment projects across Europe. content: A new strategy to combat trafficking in human beings will focus on 6 priorities: better use of technology to detect trafficking, working more closely with businesses, stepping up action against organised crime, addressing migration risks, improving crisis preparedness, and supporting people at risk.

title: Winners of 2026 Megalizzi–Niedzielski prize for aspiring journalists announced
content: Yoana Kaloyanova (Bulgaria), Žan Tone Urbanija (Slovenia), and Marie Hartmann (Germany) have won the 2026 Megalizzi–Niedzielski prize for aspiring journalists. content: Six outstanding EU-funded projects, and the people behind them, have won prizes at the EU’s 2026 REGIOSTARS Awards. title: AI adoption more than doubles in almost every EU strategic sector
content: According to a new EU analysis, the share of firms using AI in the EU’s 10 strategic sectors grew from 7% in 2021 to 18% in 2025. Media, energy and electronic sectors lead in AI adoption, while mobility, tourism and agri-food lag behind. This uneven growth is driven mainly by general-purpose AI.

title: Erasmus Days 2026: almost 11.000 events to take place across Europe
content: This week will see nearly 11.000 events take place across Europe and countries associated to the EU’s Erasmus+ programme during the 10th edition of the annual Erasmus Days. The 2026 theme ‘Learning and growing: skills for tomorrow' highlights the important role of Erasmus+ in skills development.

title: Programme for agile and rapid defence innovation gets green light
content: The new €115 million AGILE programme will provide rapid, agile and targeted financial support to small and medium-sized enterprises – including start-ups and scale-ups – to develop emerging and disruptive defence products. title: 46 new projects selected to help bolster EU’s supply of critical raw materials
content: Some 46 new strategic projects across the EU are set to bolster the EU’s supply of critical raw materials. They will help ensure that by 2030 EU capacity meets at least 10% of the EU’s annual consumption for extraction; 40% for processing and 25% for recycling of critical raw materials.

title: Updated rules to protect workers from exposure to dangerous chemicals
content: New rules will protect workers from exposure to harmful chemicals by setting new limit values for chemicals used in the battery, steel, chemical and textile industries. They also make clearer provisions for personal protective equipment. The measures should prevent around 1,700 lung cancer cases.

title: Returns to be made more effective
content: New rules aim to make returns more effective for people with no right to stay in the EU, introducing a European return order and opening the possibility of return hubs outside the EU. They complement the EU’s existing pact on migration and asylum and will aid its implementation.

title: €210 million boost to support over 700 researchers to build their careers in Europe
content: More than 700 additional researchers will be able to build their careers in Europe thanks to a boost of over €210 million to the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions – one of Europe's flagship programmes for research careers. The 2026 MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships received a record 21,627 applications.
